import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Data Cleaning and Preparation
# Get the total count of each primary dog breed
breed_counts = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts()

# Identify the top N breeds (e.g., top 15) to focus the visualization
# This helps in creating a readable heatmap by avoiding too many categories
top_n = 15
top_n_breeds = breed_counts.head(top_n).index.tolist()

# Filter the DataFrame to include only these top breeds and relevant columns
df_filtered = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_n_breeds)][['KreisLang', 'Rasse1Text']]

# Create a cross-tabulation (contingency table) of breeds per district
# This sums up the occurrences of each top breed in each district
breed_district_counts = pd.crosstab(df_filtered['KreisLang'], df_filtered['Rasse1Text'])

# Normalize the counts within each district (row-wise) to get proportions.
# This allows for comparison of breed popularity across districts,
# regardless of the total number of dogs in each district.
breed_district_proportions = breed_district_counts.div(breed_district_counts.sum(axis=1), axis=0)

# Reorder the columns (breeds) based on overall popularity for better visual consistency
breed_district_proportions = breed_district_proportions[top_n_breeds]

# Set up the matplotlib figure for the heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))

# Create the heatmap
sns.heatmap(
    breed_district_proportions,
    cmap='viridis',  # A perceptually uniform colormap
    annot=False,     # Do not annotate values to prevent clutter
    fmt=".2f",       # Format annotations if they were used
    linewidths=.5,   # Add lines between cells for better separation
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Proportion of Breed within District'} # Label for the color bar
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title(f'Proportion of Top {top_n} Dog Breeds Across Zurich Districts', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Dog Breed', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Zurich District', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability, especially for long breed names
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(rotation=0, fontsize=10)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
